provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Fabricators sell to homeowners and builders, so copy runs two page sets: slab yard and template timeline for homeowners, accounts and lead times for builders. No quartz or stone brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: In-stock slabs by material and colour, remnants sized for vanities and bar tops, how to put a slab on hold, and visiting the yard to pick the actual slab
pageStructurePlus.why: Stone buyers want to see the exact slab, not a sample chip. An inventory page is what gets them to the yard and holding a slab.

pageStructurePlus.section: Quartz, granite, marble and quartzite compared
pageStructurePlus.contains: Heat, stains, etching and scratches, sealing schedules, how seams show in veined stone, and which material suits a busy family kitchen versus a powder room
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers arrive torn between quartz and natural stone. A plain comparison makes the fabricator the advisor rather than the order-taker.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Cabinets set and level first, template day, digital templating, fabrication days, install day, sink and cooktop cutouts, plumber reconnect, and how long the kitchen is without a counter
pageStructurePlus.why: The question every countertop buyer asks is how long. A clear timeline wins against fabricators who answer it vaguely.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Edge profiles from eased to ogee, undermount and farmhouse sinks, faucet and soap holes, waterfall ends, full-height stone backsplashes and outlet cutouts
pageStructurePlus.why: The details are where tickets grow. Showing edges and waterfalls on real kitchens is how buyers decide to add them.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Account set-up for builders and remodelers, spec sheets and standard colour packages, lead times by volume, multi-unit scheduling and a bid request for plans
pageStructurePlus.why: Builders are half of a fabricator's business and decide on lead time and reliability. They need their own page set, separate from homeowners.

designDirections.name: Template Tomorrow
designDirections.bestFor: Small fabrication shops that win kitchens on a fast quote from a sketch and a short template-to-install time
designDirections.headlineSample: Quartz and granite countertops fabricated in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Indigo on white with a clean grotesque feels exact, like a cut sheet, and the page goes straight to the sketch quote form.

designDirections.name: Slab Yard
designDirections.bestFor: Fabricators with a slab yard and remnants who want buyers browsing inventory before they visit
designDirections.headlineSample: Browse in-stock slabs and remnants, cut in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Olive Grove keeps a warm natural palette with an accent that passes, and its bookish serif suits a stone catalogue.

designDirections.name: Book-Matched
designDirections.bestFor: High-end fabricators doing book-matched marble, quartzite waterfalls and designer stone work
designDirections.headlineSample: Book-matched marble and quartzite, fabricated in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Near-black with a Didone display makes veining glow like a gallery print, which is how a designer wants exotic stone presented.

openers.line: Your fabrication shop shows up on Maps for countertops in {City}, but there's no website to tap. Nobody can see a slab or a finished kitchen before calling.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a countertop buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing goes to a Facebook page. Someone choosing between quartz and granite wants to browse slabs and get a quote from a sketch, not scroll through posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest countertop job there.
openers.linkLine: A countertop page that takes a kitchen sketch: {demo-link}

openers.line: The stone site on your listing has a free-host banner and the slab gallery is clearly old stock. Buyers who drive over expecting those slabs will be disappointed.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for banners, old dates or stale inventory. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Your fabrication shop with current slabs: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your granite gallery shrinks every slab to a thumbnail, so the veining is gone. Stone is bought on the veining.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Slabs you can zoom into on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Countertops can be roughly quoted from a kitchen sketch with measurements. There's no way to send you one except email to a generic inbox or a call.
openers.hook: Check for any form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A countertop quote form that takes a sketch and measurements: {demo-link}

openers.line: You post remnants now and then, and they sell. A remnant page that stays up would sell vanity and bar-top stone every week instead of whenever you remember.
openers.hook: Look for any remnant post. If they have one, mention it.
openers.linkLine: A stone remnant page that stays current: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention seams you can't find and a quartz install done the day after template. That's the reassurance a countertop buyer needs, and it lives only on Maps.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about seams, speed or the install crew. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the countertops: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every autumn people want new countertops before they host the holidays, and the fabrication lead time decides it. The shop they find in September gets those kitchens.
openers.hook: Use this August to October. Mention the holiday deadline in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A countertop site ready for the holiday deadline: {demo-link}

openers.line: People shop for granite and quartz on Saturdays, often when your yard is closed. If they can browse slabs and hold one online, they don't drive to the next fabricator.
openers.hook: Check their hours and whether there's any online inventory. If closed weekends and nothing online, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A slab browse-and-hold page for weekends: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a stone installer. Experienced fabricators and setters look at a shop's work and equipment before they leave their current yard.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date and role.
openers.linkLine: A stone fabrication site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You install countertops across {City}, but a homeowner in {Neighborhood} can't tell if you deliver and install that far.
openers.hook: Find towns named in reviews or posts. Use the furthest.
openers.linkLine: A countertop page for each town you install in: {demo-link}

openers.line: Builders and remodelers pick a stone fabricator on lead time and reliability. A page for contractor accounts and bids would bring that work in without a sales call.
openers.hook: Look for builder tags or multi-unit posts. If any, lead with this.
openers.linkLine: A builder and contractor page for your fabrication shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: Buyers torn between quartz and marble worry about etching and sealing. A plain comparison page makes your shop the advisor they trust with the slab.
openers.hook: Check whether they ever explain material differences. If not, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A quartz versus natural stone page for your shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: Looks like most of your stone work comes through cabinet shops and remodelers. That's steady until they slow down, and direct homeowners pay better.
openers.hook: Look for posts tagging the same contractors repeatedly. Name one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where direct countertop buyers would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Those seams on the {specific recent job} are nearly invisible. Stone work like that ought to open your page, ahead of anything a countertop shopper scrolls past.
openers.hook: Pick their newest install and name the material, edge and room.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is lovely stone work.

I was looking for countertop fabricators in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no site where someone can browse slabs, send a kitchen sketch, or set up a builder account. I put together a sample fabrication site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, bumping this in case it got buried. Here's the sample countertop site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a slab and remnant page, a quote form that takes a sketch and measurements, a template-to-install timeline, and a separate page for builder accounts. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for countertop fabricators here in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a slab and remnant page, a sketch quote form and a builder account page, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many material pages and how much inventory you want listed, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes, including keeping remnants current. For a shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one kitchen of quartz."
"Is the homeowner side or the builder side the bigger priority? We'd lead with that."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and the deposit invoice, and we'll start by listing your current remnants."

objections.objection: My work comes through cabinet shops and builders.
objections.handler: "Then the builder page leads: accounts, lead times and a bid form. Direct homeowners are the higher-margin extra when builders slow down."

objections.objection: Inventory changes too fast to keep online.
objections.handler: "That's why the care plan includes it. You text me a photo of a new slab or remnant, it's up the same day. Sold ones come down."

objections.objection: People just want the cheapest quartz.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones who care about seams, edges and getting it done before the holidays. That's where your margin is."

objections.objection: I'm already listed on a lead platform.
objections.handler: "Shared leads go to several fabricators and you pay either way. Your own site sends that kitchen to one shop, you."

objections.objection: We tried a website once and it did nothing.
objections.handler: "Most stone sites are a logo and a contact page. This one has a remnant page and a sketch quote form, which is what buyers actually use."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: slabs and remnants, a sketch quote form, a timeline page and a builder page. Less than one kitchen of quartz."

email.subject: Countertop site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for countertop shops in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}, with a remnant page. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} countertop demo down on Friday.

Keep it up? One word is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, it's getting close to the pre-holiday countertop rush, when lead time decides who gets the kitchen. Thought of you.

The countertop site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Peg the build to less than one kitchen of mid-range quartz, never to an hourly rate.
Two audiences means two page sets. Quote the builder account pages as their own line, never inside the homeowner build.
A remnant page only works if it stays current. Price updates into the care plan, or quote a monthly inventory line.
A quote form that takes a sketch, measurements and sink and edge choices is the homeowner core. Price richer intake separately.
Only quote exotic stone and book-matching pages for shops that actually handle those slabs.
Launch by late summer so it ranks before the pre-holiday rush.

lineItems.description: Max with filters by material, colour and size, a hold-request button and sold tagging.
Max when they add many new slabs and remnants each week with photos and sizes.

lineItems.item: Sketch quote form with sink and edge options
lineItems.description: Max with sketch upload, measurement fields, edge, sink and backsplash options and routing.
Max with spec sheets, colour packages, lead times, plan upload and an account application.
Max when it covers quartz, granite, marble, quartzite and porcelain slab with care notes.
Max when each page has its own finished kitchens and a local review.

whatElseYouSell.name: Slab and installed-kitchen photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Full-slab shots in the yard plus three installed kitchens in good light. Veining sells stone, and phone photos flatten it."

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for countertop installs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A new quartz or granite install on your Google profile each week, captioned with the stone and the town."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review request after install day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Once the sink's reconnected and they've cooked on the new counter, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Weekly remnant sale posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every week the newest stone remnants go out as posts and an email to past buyers. Remnants sold are offcuts turned into vanity jobs."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the remnant page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Builder spec book and colour package sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed and digital countertop spec book with your standard colour packages, for builders and design centres to hand buyers."

whatElseYouSell.name: Pre-holiday countertop campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A September push for 'new counters before the holidays' with your real template-to-install time fills October."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run in September.

whatElseYouSell.name: Showroom and yard signage refresh
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Labels on every slab with material, size and a code that opens its page, so a Saturday browser can hold it from the yard."

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Counters go on the cabinets they set. The cabinet shop you template behind needs a site, and your stone is in every photo."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Consecutive trades on every kitchen; the cabinet shop buys a bigger site.

withoutAI.route: Plumbers who reconnect sinks after install
withoutAI.whoPays: The plumber, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who reconnects the sink after your install? I'll build their site, and your timeline page links to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Every install needs a plumber; the referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.whoPays: The tile setter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every quartz install ends with the homeowner asking who does tile. Give that setter a proper site and they'll send stone buyers back."
"Designers who bring clients to your yard need portfolio sites, and your stone is the centrepiece of their kitchens."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers buy on looks and already work with the fabricator.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The slab warehouse you buy from sells to fabricators across the region. A find-a-fabricator page and slab gallery would serve all of them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have budgets and their fabricator list is your prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The outdoor kitchen builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Outdoor kitchens need stone tops too. The builders who send you those slabs need sites of their own."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A second stream of stone work and a natural referral.

withAI.pitchLine: "When the cabinet shop finalises a layout, the tool drafts the countertop square footage and sends a quote request to one fabricator."
withAI.whyItWorks: It speeds the cabinet shop's close and routes stone to your client.

withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers photograph their kitchen and see it with three of the distributor's slabs before visiting a fabricator."
withAI.whyItWorks: It moves slabs and sends buyers to the distributor's fabricators.

withAI.pitchLine: "The designer enters cabinet colour and hardware, and gets slab, backsplash and edge pairings to show the client."
withAI.whyItWorks: Pairing is the slow part of kitchen design.

withAI.pitchLine: "When the fabricator books an install, the bot offers the homeowner the plumber's reconnect slot the same day."
withAI.whyItWorks: No more kitchens without a working sink for a week.

withAI.pitchLine: "From the countertop drawing it drafts the backsplash square footage, so the tile quote goes out the day the stone goes in."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fast quotes win the backsplash; the data already exists.

withAI.route: Outdoor kitchen builder's stone spec chatbot
withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers ask which stone handles sun and freezing nights. A chatbot trained on the builder's answers handles it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Material questions slow outdoor kitchen sales.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back from the saw floor
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The bridge saw is loud and the phone goes unanswered. Callers get a text asking for a kitchen sketch and the stone they're considering."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Countertop price estimator by square foot and material
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter counter lengths, pick quartz or granite level, sink and edge, and see a range before sending the sketch."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price groups by material, edge and cutout prices, and minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Review replies that name the stone
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A happy note about a new quartzite island gets a reply drafted that mentions the slab, waiting for your approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit at slab hold
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a buyer holds a slab online, the deposit link goes out and the slab is tagged as held in the yard."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their hold policy and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Live slab and remnant inventory
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Photograph a new slab, enter material and size, and it's on the site; mark it sold and it's gone. The yard and the web stay in sync."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their slab tagging method and a phone in the yard.

softwareAI.name: Kitchen-photo slab visualiser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads their kitchen and sees it with three of your in-stock slabs before visiting the yard."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs current slab photos and installed kitchens to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Template-to-install job board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every countertop job from quote to template, cut, polish and install on one board, with the plumber reconnect noted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stages, saw capacity and install crews.

softwareAI.name: Sketch-to-square-footage takeoff
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a hand sketch or a cabinet drawing and it drafts countertop square footage, seams and cutouts for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past sketches with final measured totals. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Builder account portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Builders submit countertop orders by lot with colour package and template date, and see status without calling the shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for fabricators with builder accounts. Needs their packages and lead times.

softwareAI.name: Weekend slab question assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "On weekends it answers 'do you have white quartz in stock' from live inventory, and books a yard visit or a template date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the inventory is live. Needs their FAQ and calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Template and install reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners get a text before template day to have cabinets set and the sink on site, and before install to clear the counters."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their prep checklist.

softwareAI.name: Cut optimisation and remnant tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan cuts across slabs to save stone, and every offcut becomes a sized remnant on the site automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their slab sizes and typical layouts.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on quartz versus natural stone care
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'will marble etch' and 'do I need to seal quartz' at midnight, from your own stone care notes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their care notes and lead time. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sealing reminder for natural stone customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after a granite or marble install, customers get a sealing reminder with a booking link. Small repeat stone visits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past natural stone jobs with dates and a sealing price.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by material and slab yield
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which stones and jobs actually make money once slab waste, saw time and install crews are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs slab invoices and job hours.

softwareAI.name: Material and edge page writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month a page like 'quartzite waterfall islands', drafted from your countertop jobs and approved before it's live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Slab distributor price and stock sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the distributor changes slab prices or stock, the countertop estimator and the special-order list update."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the distributor's price list format.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote at the template visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Say the runs, the sink, the edge and the backsplash during the visit, and it drafts the countertop quote for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Install photo and seam log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Installers photograph seams, overhangs and the finished countertop before leaving, so disputes have a record and the gallery fills."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their install checklist.

softwareAI.name: Fabricator and installer applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've run a saw, polished edges or set stone, so you only call real fabricators."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the slab inventory tool for fabricators
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every fabricator has slabs and remnants nobody can see online. The inventory tool I built for one shop works for any of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Inventory is the same problem in every yard; a monthly tool spreads easily.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fabricator locator for a slab distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who fall for a slab at the warehouse need a fabricator. A locator of the distributor's customers keeps the slab sold."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors only win when slabs get fabricated.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified fabricator program for a quartz maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Quartz makers need warranty registration and a certified fabricator map. I've built that workflow inside a fabrication shop."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund channel programs and need someone who knows the fabricator side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give member fabricators an inventory page, a sketch quote form and a care page as a benefit of joining."
"Agencies rarely build slab inventory well. License my countertop template with inventory and sketch quotes built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell the finished module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Builders with many lots order countertops by plan and package through one portal, routed to their fabricator."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders pay to cut coordination; you already know the stone side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Multifamily and hospitality countertop bid site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Fabricators bidding apartments and hotels need a capability site with capacity, past projects and spec downloads."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Commercial buyers check capability online before inviting bids.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One remnant site for a metro's fabricators lets vanity and bar-top buyers search every yard's offcuts at once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Remnants are dead stock; pooling them sells more for everyone.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Fabricators share their slab invoices and lead times and get back a monthly picture of where stone costs are going, built only from what they sent."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Kitchen and bath showroom fabricator handoff
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Showrooms selling cabinets need to hand buyers to a fabricator. A handoff page with slab browsing keeps the kitchen on schedule."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Showrooms want the whole kitchen finished, not stalled at the countertop.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A fabrication client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Stone yards serve their own metro. The inventory-and-sketch template moves to a fabricator a metro away from {City}."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The fabricator with a dated site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Stone shop sites with old slab galleries mislead buyers. I move them onto a live-inventory template quickly."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Easy to sell once they see their own stale inventory.

upsellLadder.offer: Countertop site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Countertop site and care plan on one contract, so a new remnant goes up the day you text me a photo."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first remnant sold through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "That remnant sold from the page. Let's post every new offcut weekly."

upsellLadder.trigger: A dramatic slab arrives or they finish a waterfall island.
upsellLadder.line: "That quartzite waterfall should lead the countertop gallery. Let's shoot it properly."

upsellLadder.trigger: They're texting new slab photos more than once a week.
upsellLadder.line: "You're adding stone faster than texts can keep up. Let the yard update the site directly."

upsellLadder.offer: Countertop price estimator by square foot and material
upsellLadder.trigger: Ninety days of sketch requests show price questions before anything else.
upsellLadder.line: "Most countertop sketches come with 'roughly how much'. The estimator answers first."

upsellLadder.trigger: A new builder account comes in through the builder page.
upsellLadder.line: "The builder page brought an account. Let's give builders a stone portal so orders don't live in texts."

upsellLadder.offer: Sealing reminder for natural stone customers
upsellLadder.trigger: A year of granite and marble installs since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "Last year's granite kitchens are due for sealing. Each reminder is a visit and a vanity remnant sale."
